structure: Part 2 read, in full, the high-risk plants journey wiring under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear: flow/flow.js (the 9 sections and FLOW_ONLY_KEYS, with the ordering rationale in its comment), flow/run.js (RUN_STEPS, the opening run, and nextRunTarget), flow/task-rows.js (7 task rows and rowStatus), flow/entry-guard.js (the deep-link guard), flow/section-captions/index.js with its English and Welsh copy (5 caption sections), features/index.js (13 dispatch pages and 17 route groups), features/evaluation.js (10 evaluation bindings), the hub feature (controller.js with its 4 GROUPS and status tags, template.njk, copy.en.js and copy.cy.js), hub.fit.spec.js (12 tests), section-caption.fit.spec.js (2 tests), obligations/index.js (25 obligations in the set) and src/server/app/routes-high-risk-plants.js (how the set mounts and wires the flow). To word the hub's blocked-row and row-entry behaviour, the platform helpers it calls were glanced at (shared/paths.js for route paths, flow/navigation.js for rowEntry/rowGatePasses/sectionEntry, bridge/status for the five status values, flow/run-state.js for the run record); claims resting on them say so in the ref. It covers the page order, the opening run and where Continue goes after each step, every task row and how its status is worked out, the entry guard and what fires it, every section caption in English and Welsh, the Overview hub page (route, heading, groups, rows, status tags, button and back link, copy in both languages) with every fit test, and the registered routes, dispatch pages and obligation list. Each section's own pages and obligation section files are left to the parts that own them.

claims.statement: The commodity details (entry) sub-page sits in a section of its own, so Continue on the commodities list page leaves the commodity section rather than running on into the details page; the details page is reached from the list and returns to it.
claims.quote:
The commodity entry sub-page sits in a section of its own rather than after
 * the list page it belongs to. `nextInSection` sends a page's Continue to the
 * next page in the same section, and the list page's Continue leaves the
 * commodity section altogether — the entry page is reached from the list and
 * returns to it, never by continuing past it.

claims.statement: The commodity details sub-page's own section still gives it the commodity-type prerequisite that every page after the entry question carries.
claims.quote:
Its own section still gives it
 * the commodity-type prerequisite that every page after the entry question
 * carries.

claims.statement: Origin comes after the commodity details sub-page, because the origin answer is enforced at Continue for every page after it, and placing it earlier would stop a trader adding a commodity line until they had named a country.
claims.quote:
Origin follows the entry sub-page rather than preceding it. Its answer is
 * enforced at Continue, so every page placed after it needs one; ahead of the
 * entry sub-page it would stop a trader adding a commodity line until they had
 * named a country.

claims.statement: The arrival section opens on the arrival status question, whose answer decides what the rest of the section asks for, and goes on to the arrival details page.
claims.quote:
The arrival section opens on the arrival-status question, whose answer
 * decides what the rest of the section asks for, and goes on to the arrival
 * details.

claims.statement: Potato notifications never see the arrival status question: it is out of scope for them, so both the opening run and the hub's arrival row skip it and land on arrival details, which every commodity type answers.
claims.quote:
Potato notifications never see the question: `arrivalStatus` is out
 * of scope for them, so the derived page gate fails and both the opening run
 * and the arrival row's hub entry (`rowGatePasses`/`rowEntry`) pass it over,
 * landing on arrival-details instead — a page every commodity type answers.

claims.statement: The place of destination is a section of its own after the arrival section, so Continue on arrival details leaves the arrival section rather than running on into the destination page.
The arrival status is not a prerequisite of the place of destination page: a trader entering from the hub with no status answered gets the pre-arrival question, which is what the page falls back to.
claims.quote:
The opening run asks the arrival status ahead of it — that order is `RUN_STEPS`
 * in run.js, not this array — so the page usually has a status to work from and
 * shows the right one of its three questions. It is not a prerequisite: a
 * trader entering from the hub with no status answered gets the pre-arrival
 * question, which is what the page falls back to.

claims.statement: A task row's status is worked out from every answer its pages collect, and is one of five values: not applicable, not started, in progress, fulfilled (completed) or optional.
claims.quote:
export const rowParts = (row) =>
  row.parts ?? row.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

export const rowStatus = (row, answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  statusOf(rowParts(row), answers, inScope, evaluation)
claims.note: The five values are defined in the platform's bridge/status/vocabulary.js: 'not-applicable', 'not-started', 'in-progress', 'fulfilled', 'optional'.

claims.statement: A row with no answer in scope for this notification is not applicable; with required answers, it is fulfilled when every required answer is satisfied, in progress when something is started, otherwise not started; with no required answers, it is optional until something is started, then fulfilled or in progress.
claims.note: Read from the platform status helper the set's rowStatus calls; the helper itself is outside the set's folders.
